Brief Hospital Course:
SUMMARY/ASSESSMENT: Mr. ___ is an ___ male with 
history of A. fib on anticoagulation, peripheral vascular 
disease status post bypass graft ___ years ago, chronic kidney 
disease, who is transferred from ___ with concern for 
cholangitis, now s/p ERCP with stent placement. Following the 
procedure, patient developed acute shortness of breath requiring 
nonrebreather briefly. He was given Lasix 20 mg IV once. He was 
weaned from O2, however has required O2 at night while sleeping. 


ACUTE/ACTIVE PROBLEMS:
# Concern for cholangitis
# s/p ERCP with stent placement 
Patient presenting with abdominal pain (the patient currently 
denies), possible low-grade fever, and overall weakness and 
bloating, concerning for cholangitis. Patient is now status post 
ERCP with stent placement, no sphincterotomy.
- on regular diet as tolerate
- has been on Abx coverage with ceftriaxone + Flagyl. No Cipro 
was given due to concern for prolonged QTC (see below). Will 
transition to PO meds: Cefpodoxime and Flagyl 
- Will need repeat ERCP in 4 weeks for stent removal and 
re-evaluation 

# Lower extremity weakness and pain
Patient initially presenting with concern for lower extremity 
weakness, cramping in his anterior thighs, similar to prior 
symptoms from peripheral vascular disease prior to his bypass. 
Patient was evaluated by vascular surgery in the emergency 
department, they indicated no need for acute surgical 
intervention. Reassuringly on exam has shown normal strength and 
sensation of the lower extremities. Feelings of weakness may be 
related to
intra-abdominal infection as above.
- continue to monitor exam
- ___ consult 
- will hold off on CTA (but could obtain with runoff if needed
given CKD to further evaluate )

# Nocturnal hypoxia.
# Hypoxic respiratory distress, improved
Patient noted to have an O2 sat of 88% on room air, and 
following the ERCP required facemask to 100% satting in the ___ 
initially per report. Was given a dose of Lasix due to concern 
for flash pulmonary edema, and his hypoxia improved. O2 was 
weaned in the morning. PE felt to be unlikely given systemic 
anticoagulation with apixaban. However, he again developed 
hypoxia overnight and was placed on O2 NC, which was weaned once 
he awoke in the morning. I suspect OSA, and would recommend 
outpatient sleep study. 
- Currently satting mid to high ___ on RA. Will ambulate patient 
to ensure he does not require O2. 
- Recommend outpatient sleep study to evaluate for OSA.

# Troponemia 
Patient found to have elevated troponin to 0.06 in ED. He did 
initially report feelings of "having a heart attack", 
indigestion and pain to scapula. Symptoms completely resolved 
following ERCP. Trops trended down. EKG in ED with no signs of 
acute ischemia. No further inpatient workup planned.

# Initial concern for QTc noted, however patient has RBBB and 
corrected QTc is appropriate <500. 
- resumed amio.
- ok to resume home trazodone
- monitored on tele, no concerning findings.

CHRONIC/STABLE PROBLEMS:
# Atrial fibrillation, with history of stroke. Patient has been 
in sinus bradycardia. 
- resumed amiodarone
- Continued home apixaban 2.5 mg bid

#Hypertension. 
- Held home lisinopril while inpatient. He has been 
normotensive, would resume at discharge.

# BPH
- continue home tamsulosin 

# Chronic kidney disease stage III. Cr on admission 1.8, 
baseline 1.6-1.8
- avoid nephrotoxic medications
- Calcitriol 0.25 mcg PO DAILY 

# PVD
- continue home aspirin 81mg
- continue home atorvastatin 20mg 

# Transitional issues
- ___ scan showing - 1 cm hyperenhancing lesion in the 
right lobe of the liver most likely representing a cavernous 
hemangioma. This could be further characterized by MRI if 
clinically indicated.
- Repeat CBC, LFTs in ___ weeks.
- Will need repeat ERCP in 4 weeks for stent removal and 
re-evaluation 
- will need cholecystectomy in 2 weeks per General Surgery 
recommendations.
